questions.stem: Commerce is best described as
options: trade and all the services that aid trade
the manufacture of goods in factories
the buying of goods for personal use only
questions.explanation: Commerce = trade + aids to trade (banking, insurance, transport, etc.).

questions.stem: The main function of commerce is to
options: convert raw materials into finished goods
extract natural resources from the earth
bridge the gap between producers and consumers
questions.explanation: Commerce links production with consumption by removing hindrances of place, time, risk, finance and knowledge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a branch of commerce?
questions.explanation: Mining, farming and manufacturing are industrial occupations; trade is a branch of commerce.

questions.stem: Transport removes the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Transport moves goods from where they are produced to where they are needed.

questions.stem: Warehousing helps to remove the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Storage makes goods available when they are needed.

questions.stem: The hindrance of knowledge (ignorance) in commerce is removed mainly by
questions.explanation: Advertising informs consumers about the existence and qualities of goods.

questions.stem: Insurance as an aid to trade removes the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Insurance spreads the risk of loss among many people.

questions.stem: Banking assists commerce mainly by
options: moving goods from place to place
providing finance and a means of payment
questions.explanation: Banks provide credit and payment services that remove the hindrance of finance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of commerce?
options: It is concerned with the distribution and exchange of goods and services
It deals only with the production of raw materials
It does not involve any risk
It is carried out only by government
questions.explanation: Commerce focuses on distribution and exchange.

questions.stem: Which of the following combinations consists entirely of aids to trade?
questions.explanation: Aids to trade include banking, insurance, transport, communication, advertising, warehousing and tourism; farming, mining and manufacturing are industry.

questions.stem: Commerce is part of
questions.explanation: Commercial services belong to the tertiary sector.

questions.stem: Communication removes the hindrance of
options: distance in passing information between buyers and sellers
questions.explanation: Telephone, post and the internet allow buyers and sellers to exchange information.

questions.stem: A major contribution of commerce to the development of a nation is that it
options: widens markets and encourages large-scale production
questions.explanation: By reaching more consumers, commerce encourages specialisation and large-scale production.

questions.stem: Occupation refers to
options: the place where a person lives
any lawful activity in which a person engages to earn a living
questions.explanation: An occupation is a legitimate means of livelihood.

questions.stem: The three broad types of occupation are
questions.explanation: Occupations are classified as industrial, commercial or services.

questions.stem: A fisherman is engaged in
questions.explanation: Extractive occupations obtain resources from nature.

questions.stem: Building houses and roads is classified as
questions.explanation: Construction industry erects buildings, roads and bridges.

questions.stem: Doctors, lawyers and hairdressers render
questions.explanation: Direct services are rendered personally to individuals who pay for them.

questions.stem: Police officers and soldiers are said to render
questions.explanation: Indirect services benefit the community and are paid for by government.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor that determines the choice of an occupation?
questions.explanation: Education, capital, interest, income and environment influence occupational choice.

questions.stem: The conversion of cotton into cloth is an example of
questions.explanation: Manufacturing changes raw materials into finished goods.

questions.stem: A woman who buys tomatoes from farmers and sells them in the market is engaged in a
questions.explanation: Buying and selling (trade) is a commercial occupation.

questions.stem: Genetic industries are those concerned with
options: the rearing of plants and animals for reproduction
questions.explanation: Genetic industry breeds crops and animals, e.g. poultry and fish farming, nurseries.

questions.stem: Which of these is an importance of occupation?
options: It provides income for the individual
questions.explanation: People earn a living through their occupations.

questions.stem: A bank clerk belongs to which occupational group?
questions.explanation: Banking is an aid to trade and so a commercial occupation.

questions.stem: The four factors of production are
questions.explanation: Land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.

questions.stem: The reward for labour is
questions.explanation: Labour earns wages.

questions.stem: Interest is the reward for
questions.explanation: Capital earns interest.

questions.stem: The entrepreneur is responsible for
options: organising the other factors of production and bearing risks
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur combines the factors and bears risk.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of labour?
options: It cannot be separated from the labourer
questions.explanation: Labour is human effort and is inseparable from the worker.

questions.stem: Mining and lumbering are examples of
questions.explanation: They extract natural resources.

questions.stem: The production of furniture from timber is
questions.explanation: Processing raw materials into finished goods is secondary production.

questions.stem: Tertiary production consists of
questions.explanation: Trade, aids to trade and direct and indirect services.

questions.stem: Division of labour is most beneficial to a firm when
options: the product is made by one craftsman
there is a large market for its product
questions.explanation: Specialisation requires a large market to absorb the bigger output.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of specialisation to a nation is
options: over-dependence on other countries for some goods
questions.explanation: Specialising nations rely on others for what they do not produce.

questions.stem: Specialisation by process means that
options: each country produces the goods it is best at
each worker concentrates on a particular stage in the making of a product
each firm produces only one product
each worker makes the complete product
questions.explanation: Process specialisation splits production into stages.

questions.stem: Capital as a factor of production includes
questions.explanation: Capital is man-made aids to production.

questions.stem: Which factor of production is described as the most mobile?
options: Unskilled labour in a remote village
questions.explanation: Money capital can be moved easily; land is immobile.

questions.stem: Production is said to be complete when
questions.explanation: Production includes distribution to the final consumer.

questions.stem: Home trade refers to
options: buying and selling of goods within the boundaries of a country
trade carried out from home only
questions.explanation: Home (domestic) trade takes place within a country.

questions.stem: The two branches of home trade are
questions.explanation: Home trade is divided into wholesale and retail.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of home trade?
options: Customs duties are charged on every sale
The same currency is used by buyers and sellers
questions.explanation: Domestic trade uses one currency and avoids customs formalities.

questions.stem: Compared with foreign trade, home trade has
questions.explanation: Home trade avoids foreign exchange, customs and language problems.

questions.stem: The chain of distribution in home trade commonly runs from
options: manufacturer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
consumer to retailer to wholesaler to manufacturer
questions.explanation: Goods flow from producer through middlemen to consumer.

questions.stem: A manufacturer who sells directly to consumers through its own outlets has
questions.explanation: Direct selling cuts out middlemen.

questions.stem: A major problem of home trade in Nigeria is
options: poor road network that raises distribution costs
questions.explanation: Poor transport infrastructure increases costs and delays.

questions.stem: Home trade contributes to national development by
options: promoting specialisation among regions within the country
questions.explanation: Different regions specialise and trade with each other.

questions.stem: A trader who buys a bag of rice and sells it in cups to households is engaged in
questions.explanation: Selling in small quantities to final consumers is retailing.

questions.stem: Middlemen in home trade include
questions.explanation: Middlemen stand between producers and final consumers.

questions.stem: The elimination of middlemen in home trade is often advocated because
options: middlemen perform no functions at all
it may reduce the final price paid by consumers
manufacturers prefer to bear storage costs
it increases the number of transactions
questions.explanation: Fewer middlemen means fewer profit mark-ups, though their functions must still be performed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of home trade?
questions.explanation: Exporting is foreign trade.

questions.stem: A retailer is a trader who
options: buys goods in bulk from manufacturers to sell to retailers
sells goods in small quantities to final consumers
questions.explanation: Retailers are the last link in the chain of distribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of a retailer to the consumer?
options: Buying goods in bulk from manufacturers
questions.explanation: Retailers break bulk to suit consumers.

questions.stem: A retailer serves the wholesaler by
options: passing on information about consumers' tastes and needs
questions.explanation: Retailers are in direct contact with consumers and feed back information.

questions.stem: A trader who moves from place to place selling goods is called
questions.explanation: Itinerant traders have no fixed shop.

questions.stem: A large shop with several sections under one roof, each selling different kinds of goods, is a
questions.explanation: Department stores combine many departments in one building.

questions.stem: A group of similar shops owned by one company and located in different towns is called
questions.explanation: Chain stores operate identical branches in different places.

questions.stem: A supermarket is characterised by
options: self-service and prices clearly marked on goods
questions.explanation: Customers serve themselves and pay at check-out points.

questions.stem: Mail order business is a form of retailing in which
options: goods are sold through vending machines
customers order goods from catalogues and receive them by post or courier
goods are hawked from house to house
goods are sold only in open markets
questions.explanation: Orders are placed remotely and goods delivered.

questions.stem: A tied shop is one that
options: is owned by a cooperative society
sells only the products of one manufacturer under an agreement
sells goods on hire purchase only
questions.explanation: Tied shops are tied to one supplier, e.g. a branded fuel outlet.

questions.stem: A major advantage of small-scale retailers over large-scale retailers is
options: personal contact with customers and willingness to give credit
questions.explanation: Small retailers know their customers personally and may sell on credit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of supermarkets?
options: Shopping is done under one roof
Customers are unable to bargain over prices
questions.explanation: Fixed prices remove the possibility of bargaining.

questions.stem: An automatic vending machine is used mainly to sell
options: small standardised items such as drinks and snacks
questions.explanation: Vending machines dispense small packaged goods.

questions.stem: Retail cooperative societies are formed mainly to
options: enable members to buy goods at fair prices and share surpluses
questions.explanation: Consumer cooperatives eliminate middlemen and distribute surpluses to members.

questions.stem: Which of these is a modern trend in retailing?
questions.explanation: E-commerce and delivery services are growing trends in retailing.

questions.stem: A kiosk is an example of a
questions.explanation: Kiosks are small fixed retail outlets.

questions.stem: A retailer buys a carton of noodles for ₦4,800 and sells it for ₦6,000. The mark-up on cost is
Using the same figures (cost ₦4,800, selling price ₦6,000), the retailer's margin on selling price is
questions.explanation: Margin = profit ÷ selling price × 100 = 1,200 ÷ 6,000 × 100 = 20%.

questions.stem: Hypermarkets differ from ordinary supermarkets mainly because they are
options: much larger and often located outside the town centre
questions.explanation: Hypermarkets are very large self-service stores, often with parking space on city outskirts.

questions.stem: A wholesaler is a trader who
options: buys in large quantities from producers and sells in smaller quantities to retailers
sells directly to final consumers in small units
questions.explanation: Wholesalers link manufacturers and retailers.

questions.stem: Breaking bulk means
options: buying goods in large quantities and selling in smaller quantities
questions.explanation: Wholesalers buy bulk and sell smaller lots.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a service rendered by the wholesaler to the manufacturer?
options: Selling goods in small quantities to consumers
Relieving him of the cost of storage
questions.explanation: By buying in bulk the wholesaler takes over storage and finances production.

questions.stem: A service the wholesaler renders to the retailer is
options: buying in bulk from the retailer
questions.explanation: Wholesalers often allow retailers to buy on credit.

questions.stem: The wholesaler helps to stabilise prices by
options: storing goods when supply is plentiful and releasing them in times of scarcity
fixing the prices of all goods
questions.explanation: Warehousing evens out supply over time.

questions.stem: A "cash and carry" wholesaler is one who
options: delivers goods to consumers on credit
sells to retailers who pay cash and transport the goods themselves
questions.explanation: Cash-and-carry wholesalers offer lower prices without credit or delivery.

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason for eliminating the wholesaler?
options: Manufacturers may wish to control the marketing of their products
Retailers prefer to hold very large stocks
Goods are produced in small quantities by many firms
questions.explanation: Large manufacturers may set up their own distribution to control quality and branding.

questions.stem: The wholesaler is difficult to eliminate when
options: goods are produced by many small producers scattered over a wide area
goods are highly perishable and sold locally
questions.explanation: Collecting output from many small producers requires a wholesaler.

questions.stem: A general wholesaler is one who
options: deals in only one line of goods
deals in a wide variety of goods
questions.explanation: General wholesalers stock many lines; specialised wholesalers stock one line.

questions.stem: The wholesaler is often regarded as a link between the
questions.explanation: The wholesaler stands between producers and retailers.

questions.stem: Wholesalers assist manufacturers to plan production by
options: placing orders in advance and providing market information
questions.explanation: Advance orders and feedback help manufacturers plan.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes "regional wholesalers"?
options: Wholesalers who deal only with imports
Wholesalers who sell only one product
Wholesalers who serve retailers in a particular area of the country
questions.explanation: Regional wholesalers cover a defined geographical area.

questions.stem: Grading and packaging of goods for retailers is a function of the
questions.explanation: Wholesalers often sort, grade and repack goods.

questions.stem: One reason why some retailers prefer to buy directly from manufacturers is to
options: reduce the variety of their stock
questions.explanation: Bypassing the wholesaler can lower the cost price.

questions.stem: Wholesalers who undertake the financing of production by paying manufacturers in advance are said to
questions.explanation: Prompt or advance payment releases the manufacturer's capital.

questions.stem: Merchant wholesalers differ from agent wholesalers in that merchant wholesalers
options: take ownership (title) of the goods they deal in
questions.explanation: Merchant wholesalers buy and own the goods; agents work on commission.

questions.stem: Foreign trade is the exchange of goods and services
questions.explanation: Foreign (international) trade crosses national boundaries.

questions.stem: Entrepôt trade involves
options: importing goods for local consumption only
importing goods for re-export to other countries
questions.explanation: Entrepôt (re-export) trade passes imports on to other countries.

questions.stem: A bill of lading is
options: a document of title issued by a shipping company for goods carried by sea
an order sent by an importer
questions.explanation: It is evidence of the contract of carriage, a receipt and a document of title.

questions.stem: A consular invoice is required by an importing country mainly to
options: confirm the value of goods for customs purposes
questions.explanation: It is certified by the importing country's consul to verify prices for duty.

questions.stem: A certificate of origin shows
options: the country in which the goods were produced
questions.explanation: It is used for applying preferential tariffs and trade rules.

questions.stem: An indent is
options: an order for goods placed by an importer through an agent abroad
a document showing customs duty paid
an invoice sent before goods are delivered
a receipt for goods received by a ship
questions.explanation: Indents may be open (any supplier) or closed (a named supplier).

questions.stem: A closed indent is one in which
options: the agent is free to buy from any manufacturer
the importer names the particular manufacturer from whom goods are to be bought
goods are bought for cash only
questions.explanation: Closed (specific) indents specify the supplier.

questions.stem: C.I.F. in a quotation means that the price includes
options: cost of goods only at the factory
cost of goods, insurance and freight to the port of destination
customs, insurance and freight paid by the buyer
questions.explanation: CIF prices cover cost, insurance and freight to the named port.

questions.stem: Under F.O.B. terms, the seller is responsible for all costs until the goods
options: are loaded on board the ship
questions.explanation: Free On Board: the buyer bears costs after loading.

questions.stem: A letter of credit is mainly used in foreign trade to
options: assure the exporter of payment through a bank
questions.explanation: The importer's bank undertakes to pay on presentation of documents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of foreign trade?
options: Short distances between buyers and sellers
questions.explanation: Different currencies, languages, laws and long distances complicate foreign trade.

questions.stem: A ship's manifest is
options: a document showing the ship's insurance
a list of all the cargo carried by a ship
a document issued by the consul
questions.explanation: The manifest details the ship's cargo for customs.

questions.stem: Customs duty imposed on imports is intended partly to
options: protect local industries from foreign competition
questions.explanation: Import duties raise revenue and protect domestic producers.

questions.stem: The mate's receipt is issued
options: by the ship's officer as evidence that goods have been received on board
by customs after duty is paid
questions.explanation: It is later exchanged for the bill of lading.

questions.stem: Goods brought into a country from abroad are called
questions.explanation: Imports come in; exports go out.

questions.stem: A bonded warehouse is used to store
options: goods for export that have been paid for
imported goods on which customs duty has not yet been paid
questions.explanation: Duty is paid when goods are released from bond.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Export Promotion Council is mainly concerned with
questions.explanation: It promotes non-oil export development.

questions.stem: A balance of trade surplus means
options: the value of visible exports exceeds that of visible imports
questions.explanation: Balance of trade compares visible exports and imports.

questions.stem: The first document sent by a buyer to a seller to ask about prices and terms is
questions.explanation: An enquiry starts the purchase procedure.

questions.stem: A quotation is
options: a seller's reply to an enquiry, stating prices and terms
questions.explanation: Quotations give prices and conditions of sale.

questions.stem: A pro-forma invoice is sent
options: in advance, where payment is required before goods are dispatched
questions.explanation: It also serves as a quotation or for consignment and customs purposes.

questions.stem: A credit note is sent by a seller to a buyer when
options: the buyer has been overcharged or has returned goods
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount the buyer owes.

questions.stem: A debit note is issued by the seller when
options: the buyer has paid in full
questions.explanation: A debit note increases the amount owed.

questions.stem: A statement of account shows
options: transactions between buyer and seller over a period and the balance due
the country of origin of goods
questions.explanation: It summarises invoices, payments, credit and debit notes.

questions.stem: The letters E.&O.E. on an invoice mean
questions.explanation: They reserve the seller's right to correct mistakes.

questions.stem: Trade discount is allowed
options: by one trader to another, usually to enable the buyer to make a profit on resale
questions.explanation: Trade discount is a deduction from list price for traders.

questions.stem: Cash discount is given to encourage
questions.explanation: Cash discount rewards early settlement.

questions.stem: Goods with a list price of ₦250,000 were sold to a retailer subject to 10% trade discount and 5% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If the retailer paid within 14 days, the amount paid was
questions.explanation: After trade discount: ₦225,000; less 5% cash discount: ₦213,750.

questions.stem: On goods listed at ₦250,000 with 10% trade discount, the trade discount amount is

Emeka bought on credit: 60 tins of milk at ₦1,500 each, 40 packets of tea at ₦2,500 each and 25 bags of sugar at ₦4,000 each. He was allowed 20% trade discount and 2.5% cash discount, and paid within the discount period. How much did he pay?
questions.explanation: Gross = ₦290,000; after 20% trade discount = ₦232,000; after 2.5% cash discount = ₦226,200.

questions.stem: In Emeka's purchase above (gross ₦290,000, 20% trade discount, 2.5% cash discount), the cash discount received was
questions.explanation: Cash discount = 2.5% of the invoice after trade discount (₦232,000) = ₦5,800.

questions.stem: C.O.D. means that
options: goods are delivered after payment by cheque
payment is made when the goods are delivered
questions.explanation: Cash On Delivery.

questions.stem: A consignment note accompanies goods sent
options: by sea under a bill of lading only
by post as a parcel only
by a transport carrier, giving details of the goods and the parties
questions.explanation: It is issued for goods sent by road or rail carriers.

questions.stem: A warranty in a contract of sale is
options: a main term whose breach allows the contract to be cancelled
a minor term whose breach gives a right to damages only
questions.explanation: Breach of warranty entitles the buyer to damages, not repudiation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of credit sale?
questions.explanation: Hire purchase lets the buyer use goods while paying in instalments.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of credit trading to the seller is
questions.explanation: Some debtors may fail to pay.

questions.stem: The document a buyer sends to a seller to request specific goods is
questions.explanation: The order is the buyer's formal request.

questions.stem: Quantity discount is allowed to buyers who
questions.explanation: It rewards bulk purchase.

questions.stem: Legal tender refers to
options: money that must be accepted in settlement of debts
questions.explanation: Notes and coins issued by the central bank are legal tender.

questions.stem: Advertising is
options: a paid form of communicating information about goods or services to the public
the storage of goods in a warehouse
the transport of goods to consumers
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid, non-personal promotion through media.

questions.stem: Advertising that aims mainly to tell consumers about a new product and its uses is
questions.explanation: Informative advertising educates consumers about a product.

questions.stem: Advertising that is designed to convince consumers to buy one brand rather than its rivals is
questions.explanation: Competitive advertising stresses the advantages of a brand over others.

questions.stem: When an association of rice farmers advertises "Eat more local rice" without naming any brand, it is engaged in
questions.explanation: Collective advertising promotes a product type on behalf of a whole industry.

questions.stem: Advertising aimed at building the image and reputation of a company rather than selling a particular product is
questions.explanation: Institutional advertising promotes goodwill toward the organisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advertising medium?
questions.explanation: Media include press, radio, television, billboards, cinema and the internet.

questions.stem: An advantage of television as an advertising medium is that it
options: allows permanent reference like a magazine
questions.explanation: TV appeals to both sight and hearing.

questions.stem: Radio is often preferred for advertising in rural areas because it
options: reaches many people, including those who cannot read
questions.explanation: Radio is cheap, widespread and does not require literacy.

questions.stem: A major criticism of advertising is that it
options: may raise the cost of goods and mislead consumers
questions.explanation: Advertising costs are passed on to consumers and some adverts exaggerate.

questions.stem: An advantage of advertising to the manufacturer is that it
options: increases sales and makes large-scale production possible
questions.explanation: Increased demand allows economies of scale.

questions.stem: Sales promotion techniques include
options: bills of exchange and promissory notes
free samples, coupons and price discounts
questions.explanation: Sales promotions are short-term incentives to buy.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, advertisements are regulated mainly to
options: protect consumers from false or offensive messages
stop all foreign products from being advertised
ensure only government adverts are aired
questions.explanation: Regulation ensures adverts are truthful, decent and responsible.

questions.stem: An advertising agency is a firm that
options: plans and produces advertisements for clients
questions.explanation: Agencies design campaigns and buy media space.

questions.stem: Personal selling differs from advertising in that personal selling
options: involves face-to-face contact between the seller and the buyer
questions.explanation: Personal selling is individual, two-way communication.

questions.stem: Advertising in which a firm attacks the claims of a rival product directly is called
questions.explanation: Combative advertising directly challenges competitors.

questions.stem: Displaying goods attractively in shop windows to draw customers is called
questions.explanation: Window displays are a form of point-of-sale promotion.

questions.stem: A commercial bank is a financial institution that
options: accepts deposits from the public and grants loans
questions.explanation: Commercial (deposit money) banks take deposits and lend.

questions.stem: The account on which cheques can be drawn is the
questions.explanation: Cheque books are issued on current accounts.

questions.stem: A fixed (time) deposit account is one in which
options: money can be withdrawn by cheque at any time
money is deposited for an agreed period at a higher interest rate
the bank charges for keeping the money
questions.explanation: Funds are locked in for a term in return for higher interest.

questions.stem: The person who writes and signs a cheque is the
questions.explanation: The drawer instructs the bank (drawee) to pay the payee.

questions.stem: On a cheque, the drawee is the
options: bank on which the cheque is drawn
person to whom the money is paid
questions.explanation: The drawee is the bank.

questions.stem: A crossed cheque is one that
options: must be paid into a bank account and cannot be cashed over the counter
has been dishonoured by the bank
questions.explanation: Two parallel lines across the face mean it must go through an account.

questions.stem: A cheque presented for payment after it has been in circulation for longer than the period allowed by banks is
questions.explanation: Banks refuse stale cheques; the drawer must re-date or issue a new one.

questions.stem: A cheque that bears a date later than the date on which it is written is
questions.explanation: It cannot be paid until the date shown.

questions.stem: A bank may dishonour a cheque if
options: the payee has an account with another bank
the drawer has insufficient funds in the account
questions.explanation: Insufficient funds, signature mismatch or alterations can lead to dishonour.

questions.stem: A standing order is an instruction by a customer to the bank to
options: pay a fixed sum regularly to a named person on stated dates
questions.explanation: Useful for recurring payments such as rent or subscriptions.

questions.stem: A bank draft is
options: a loan granted to a customer
a cheque drawn by a bank on itself or its branch
questions.explanation: Bank drafts are guaranteed and widely accepted.

questions.stem: An overdraft allows a customer to
options: save money for a fixed period
withdraw more than the balance in a current account up to an agreed limit
borrow a fixed sum credited to a separate loan account
buy shares on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Interest is charged only on the amount overdrawn.

questions.stem: Which of these is an electronic banking service?
questions.explanation: ATMs, POS terminals, mobile and internet banking are e-banking.

questions.stem: The central bank acts as "lender of last resort" by
options: lending to individuals who are refused elsewhere
providing funds to commercial banks facing liquidity problems
questions.explanation: It supports the banking system in emergencies.

questions.stem: Credit transfer (bank giro) is a system whereby
options: the bank lends money to customers
a customer transfers ownership of shares
a debtor pays cash to the creditor at home
one cheque or instruction is used to pay several creditors through their bank accounts
questions.explanation: Many payments are made with a single instruction and transfer.

questions.stem: A specially crossed cheque bears
options: the name of a particular bank between the crossing lines
questions.explanation: Special crossing directs that payment be made only through the named bank.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of commercial banks?
questions.explanation: Commercial banks keep valuables and documents for customers.

questions.stem: The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) was established mainly to
options: protect depositors in the event of bank failure
questions.explanation: NDIC insures deposits and supervises banks.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a bank loan from an overdraft?
options: A loan attracts no interest, while an overdraft attracts interest
A loan is available only to government
An overdraft must always be secured by land
A loan is a fixed sum credited to a separate account, while an overdraft is drawn on a current account up to a limit
questions.explanation: Loans are fixed amounts repaid by instalments; overdrafts fluctuate.

questions.stem: A document used by a customer to pay cash into a bank account is a
questions.explanation: Paying-in slips record deposits.

questions.stem: Communication in commerce means
options: the carriage of goods by road
the transmission of information from one person or place to another
the buying and selling of goods
questions.explanation: Communication passes messages between parties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a postal service?
questions.explanation: Post offices offer registered mail, parcels, courier and box services.

questions.stem: Poste restante is a postal service for
options: travellers without a fixed address, who collect their mail at a named post office
questions.explanation: Mail is held at the post office for collection.

questions.stem: Registered post is used mainly for
options: sending valuable items, with proof of posting and compensation for loss
collecting mail at the post office
questions.explanation: Registration gives a record and limited compensation.

questions.stem: A private mail bag service is suitable for
options: organisations that receive large volumes of mail
people who send one letter a year
questions.explanation: Bulk mail is collected in a locked bag.

questions.stem: Electronic mail (e-mail) is sent through
questions.explanation: E-mail uses the internet.

questions.stem: Courier services are preferred by businesses because they
options: deliver documents and parcels quickly to the recipient's door
questions.explanation: Speed and door-to-door delivery are their advantages.

questions.stem: The main body that regulates the telecommunications industry in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The NCC regulates telecommunications.

questions.stem: An advantage of video conferencing to a business is that it
options: allows meetings among people in different locations without travelling
is cheaper than a phone call in every case
questions.explanation: It saves travel time and cost.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?
questions.explanation: Non-verbal communication uses body language and signs.

questions.stem: A post office box service allows
options: mail to be delivered to a locked box at the post office for collection by the renter
